take: The EIA’s 4.8 million b/d (6%) collapse in global refinery inputs in 2Q26, tied to the Middle East conflict, is the core bullish signal for products, and the Oilprice warning of a global diesel crunch lasting well into 2027 confirms that the constraint is refining capacity, not crude availability. Singapore VLSFO back above $1,000 a tonne for the first time since March, alongside Egypt doubling its LNG import bill and deferring cargoes into 2027 whilst burning fuel oil, shows the war’s second-round effects are now hitting both bunker and gas markets. The inventory angle is unambiguously tight: API reported a 5.267 million barrel draw in US crude for the week ending 30 October, extending the prior week’s fall, and with US refinery utilisation averaging above 95% between May and September — the highest since 1998 — there is little slack to rebuild product stocks. The cross-market link to watch is the gasoil–VLSFO spread: with diesel imports from the Middle East having crashed and Singapore bunkers above $1,000, any further widening pulls refining economics toward distillate yield and tightens the bunker market further. Over the next 24 hours, watch the official EIA inventory print for confirmation of the API draw, headlines from the US midterms and Trump’s comment that there is no immediate plan to strike Iran, plus any escalation from Houthi ground incursions into Saudi Arabia — all of which will set the risk premium for crude and, by extension, the whole barrel complex.

items.title: Global refinery inputs fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 before modest recovery
items.summary: Global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), or 6%, following the start of conflict in late February in the Middle East, according to data from Kpler. Throughput then increased by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, primarily as refiners in the region adjusted to new trade flows.

Colombia's government has declared a national disaster in anticipation of a drought resulting from an expected strong El Niño.

items.title: U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026

Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel, incentivizing the increased run rates.
